title: Run Summary (--json form)
description: The machine-readable form of the structured run summary (NFR-5). The DEFAULT output is human-readable prose; this JSON form is the opt-in --json output. Both ports MUST emit byte-identical JSON for identical inputs (Constitution VI, canonical serialisation per research §11).

dry_run.description: True when produced by a --dry-run twin; the action set MUST equal the real run's (FR-033).

transitioned.description: 023, data-model.md §5, FR-011: the number of tickets actually moved by a declared step. Present ONLY when the run carries a lifecycle event AND at least one role declares a step for it — a run with no event, or an event no role maps, carries no such key (byte-identical to a pre-023 summary).

actions.description: The ordered write-action set of a reconcile run; the --dry-run report equals the real run's set exactly (FR-033). URLs are host-relative — the site host is a coordinate that never appears in output (Constitution IV).

artifacts.description: 036, data-model.md §5: one entry per file of the feature directory, in the artifact set's byte-wise path order. Present ONLY when the run had an artifact set to decide about — a run outside a feature directory, or one whose set is empty, carries no such key and is byte-identical to a pre-036 summary.

path.description: Relative to the feature directory, always `/`-separated (FR-005).

attachment_name.description: The flattened name the file attaches under: path segments joined with `__` (research R7).

hash.description: The artifact's content hash. Present only on an entry the run intends to write, because the publication manifest is composed from this array and has nowhere else to record it.

action.description: `unchanged` is the zero-churn outcome and performs no write. `would-publish` / `would-revise` are the --dry-run twins of the two write actions, predicted but not performed (Constitution XI, the existing `would-` convention).

reason.description: Why the artifact was withheld. Required whenever `action` is `withheld`, and accompanied by the facts the operator needs to act on it (FR-021, Principle XVI). The first two are per-artifact decisions and carry the artifact's own facts; the last four take down the WHOLE publication and are recorded on every entry it would have written, so the summary never reports `published` for a file that reached nothing.

size.description: The artifact's size in bytes; carried by an `oversized` withholding.

limit.description: The site's DISCOVERED attachment limit in bytes, never an assumed one (Principle VII); carried by an `oversized` withholding.

collides_with.description: The other path(s) flattening to the same attachment name; carried by a `name-collision` withholding.

artifact_warnings.description: 036, T112: the publication phase's OWN warnings, carried separately from `warnings` so the default prose rendering can print them without printing every other feature's. `warnings` is written by every feature since 021 and prose has only ever shown its count; surfacing that array wholesale would change the default output of runs this feature never touched. Present only when the publication warned. Each string also appears in `warnings`, which stays the complete list.

warnings.description: Human-readable lifecycle-safety warnings (withheld transitions, drift); present only when lifecycle facts were supplied.

notes.description: Non-gating informational notes (e.g. open blocking links named per FR-037); present only when lifecycle facts were supplied.

effects.description: The effects of a /speckit.jira.config run, reported SEPARATELY (FR-054).

drift.description: Named drift warnings per ticket + divergent field (FR-031).

flags.description: Tickets carrying Jira's Flagged marker; transitions withheld by default (FR-036).

blockers.description: Open blocking links named as info, non-gating (FR-037).

provisional.description: Degraded-mode team-name proposals derived from local branch names, each flagged as unverified because Jira introspection was unavailable (030). Empty when the scan found nothing. Present only on a degraded `config` run.

rerun_guidance.description: What the operator must supply to turn a degraded run into a full one, named literally (Principle XVI). Present only on a degraded `config` run.

exit_code.description: The documented, monotonically escalating exit code (see cli-contract.md).

status.description: Every value is a WRITE outcome, because every effect writes a file this extension owns. `would_create` is the dry-run twin of `created`, predicted but not performed (Constitution XI); `inert` means the managed region exists but the run had nothing to put in it. 034 removed the five READ-ONLY values (healthy, incomplete, held_disabled, duplicated, unreadable) along with their sole producer, the hooks effect: the extension no longer reads the hook registry, so it makes no claim that a write outcome could not describe.

projects.description: The per-project style audit of the discovery effect (002 FR-003): style plus its provenance, per bound project key.
